chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
How many are the objects of lessons, but how few the taking of lessons.

key_terms.الِاعْتِبَارَ: taking of lessons / deep reflection / contemplation
key_terms.الْعِبَرَ: objects of lessons / signs to be learned from

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'How many are the objects of lessons, but how few the taking of lessons' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual malaise of his time, where the proliferation of divine signs (ʿibar) failed to translate into genuine introspection (iʿtibār). This observation underscores the Shia emphasis on *tafakkur* (contemplation) as the bridge between external observation and internal transformation, warning that mere exposure to truth is insufficient without active cognitive engagement.
